claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately states the general prohibition in 14 CFR 91.213(a) against taking off an aircraft with inoperative instruments or equipment installed unless paragraph (d) applies or conditions (1) through (5) are satisfied.
Claim C0001 faithfully represents condition (a)(1), requiring that an approved Minimum Equipment List exists for the aircraft under paragraph (a) takeoff conditions.
Claim C0002 correctly captures the first sentence of paragraph (a)(2), requiring the aircraft to have within it a letter of authorization issued by the responsible Flight Standards office.
Claim C0003 correctly represents the second sentence of paragraph (a)(2), providing that the letter of authorization may be obtained by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder.
Claim C0004 accurately records the factual statement from (a)(2) that the Minimum Equipment List and the letter of authorization constitute a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft.
Claim C0005 correctly incorporates both requirements of paragraph (a)(3) for the approved Minimum Equipment List under the paragraph (a) takeoff conditions.
Claim C0006 faithfully reflects paragraph (a)(4), requiring aircraft records available to the pilot to include an entry describing the inoperable instruments and equipment.
Claim C0007 correctly captures condition (a)(5), requiring the aircraft to be operated under all applicable conditions and limitations contained in the MEL and letter of authorization.
Claim C0008 completely and accurately covers the exclusions in paragraph (b)(1)-(3) regarding items that may not be included in a Minimum Equipment List.
Claim C0009 accurately captures the mandate in paragraph (c) for a person authorized to use an approved MEL under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use that list to comply with this section.
Claim C0010 comprehensively retains all provisions, conditions, aircraft categories, and alternatives specified under paragraph (d) for takeoff without an approved MEL.
Claim C0011 focuses specifically on the maintenance compliance duty in paragraph (d)(3)(ii) when deactivation involves maintenance, accurately reflecting the source rule.
Claim C0012 correctly states that an aircraft with inoperative instruments or equipment under paragraph (d) is considered in a properly altered condition acceptable to the Administrator.
Claim C0013 accurately reflects paragraph (e) regarding operation under a special flight permit notwithstanding any other provision of the section.
